ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=75^\circ$, $AE\perp BC$ at point E, $CD\perp AB$ at point D, $AE$ and $CD$ intersect at point F, and $\angle AFC=120^\circ$. Calculate $\angle BCD$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, triangle ABC has vertex A at the top, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right; BC is the base. Point E is on BC, and AE is drawn downward from A to E, representing the altitude from A to BC; point D is on AB, CD is drawn from C to D, and there is a right-angle mark at D, indicating that CD is perpendicular to AB. AE and CD intersect at F. The angle required in the figure is ∠BCD, formed by CB and CD at point C. Then reason: It is known that AE ⟂ BC and CD ⟂ AB, so the angle between lines AE and CD and the angle between lines BC and AB are supplementary or equal; take the obtuse angle ∠AFC in the figure. Because ∠AFC = 120°, the corresponding interior angle of the triangle ∠ABC = 180° - 120° = 60°. In triangle BCD, D is on AB, so BD and AB are collinear; also CD ⟂ AB, so ∠BDC = 90°. At the same time, ∠CBD is ∠ABC, namely 60°. Therefore ∠BCD = 180° - 90° - 60° = 30°.
